skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2, before any questions, the interviewer said the firm represents the Committee and the company, not the witness personally, and cannot give legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 states the privilege belongs to the company and that the company may decide to share what is said, including with the government.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: Only the opening warning was given. There is no explanation of ground rules, no invitation to speculate while flagging it, no request for complete answers, and no separation of recollection from uncertainty; the interviewer moved straight to T4.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asks Any questions? and T3 acknowledges understanding. The witness's remark that he may want his own counsel at T3 was not addressed.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T150 asks if there is anything else; T152 to T157 cover other witnesses and documents; T158 gives a confidentiality reminder and a keep-documents instruction. No next steps are stated.

moments.text: We represent the Committee and the company, not you personally.
This conversation is privileged, but the privilege belongs to the company
Witness said he may want his own counsel later; the interviewer did not address this.
Interviewer asked whether there was anything else the Committee should know.
Please keep any documents related to this, and don't discuss this interview with anyone.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations at T12, T24, T32 and T46 let the witness walk through LJM1, the Rhythms unwind, Chewco and the LJM2 controls.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Each topic moves from role and background to the specific deal, figures and personal interests in a sensible order.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are single and clear, but a few such as T136 combine a summary with a question.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Remained neutral and polite under evasive answers, e.g. T116 'Help me understand the difference.'

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer changed course on vague answers: the Foundation at T69 to T71, the $4.5M return at T80, the Chewco note at T132 to T136 and the Finance Committee figures at T116. It did not pursue new leads such as Glisan's invitation or the payment authorization.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Several evasions were challenged (T38, T62, T70, T80, T116, T136), but key evasive answers were left unchallenged at T45, T93, T97, T105 and T149.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Who, what, when and how are covered for LJM1, the unwind, Chewco and the $2.6M payment, though who approved the payment and who invited whom remain thin.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: Documents were used to refresh memory at T72, T98 and T132, but no other approach was tried when the witness said he did not recall (T45, T141, T147).

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked who approved and what counsel said (T40, T144), but accepted second-hand claims such as the belief that Skilling told the Board (T41) without separating personal knowledge.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: At T152 the interviewer asked who else to speak with, and the witness named Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper and the outside firms.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: At T154 and T156 the interviewer asked about deal files and personal notes and emails, and documents were shown at T72, T98 and T132.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Approximations were requested (T62, T80), but the interviewer did not test I don't recall or may have answers (T45, T141, T143, T149).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Most material answers were followed up, but more than two key leads were never followed up (T53, T57, T85, T93, T105, T149, T157), which caps this skill at 2.

skills.reason: Challenged many contradictions, but left key evasions unchallenged: 'market terms' versus negotiating Southampton himself (T83, T89), 'I may have said it should be resolved' (T149), and 'Being informed isn't the same as negotiating' (T137).

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.reason: Covers who, what, when and how for the LJM1 origin, Rhythms unwind, Chewco, LJM2 controls and the $2.6M payment, with dates and amounts such as T80 and T112.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.reason: Uses documents to refresh memory: the Southampton agreement (T72), LJM2 investor report (T98-T100) and Kopper note (T132). Did not use the approval sheet when the witness said he would have to look (T53).

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.reason: Asked whether he was on the Nov 5 call (T42) and who knew about Kopper (T40), but did not separate personal knowledge from 'I understand' or 'I believe' statements such as T129 and T41.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.reason: T152 asks who else to speak with and the witness names Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and V&E. Did not pursue McMahon or Mordaunt as witnesses.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.reason: T154-T156 asks for documents and identifies approval sheets, Board materials, partnership agreements, and personal notes and emails.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.reason: Tested 'high teens' and 'a few million' (T64, T79-T80), but did not test hedges like 'may have' (T97, T149) or 'I don't recall' (T45, T141).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.reason: Followed up most material answers, but at least two key leads (T53 approvals papered after closing; T149 possible authorization of the payment) were never pursued, capping this skill.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.reason: Documents were shown with some context, e.g. T72 and T98, but there was no pre-showing recall question and little authentication of the handwritten note (T132).

skills.name: Narrative
skills.reason: Asked the witness what the LJM2 report figures were before he explained (T98-T100), and put $4.5M to him from 'our information' before his own account (T80).

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.reason: Descriptions match the record: the $25,000 and $4.5M Foundation figures (T74, T80), LJM2 returns of 193, 278 and 2,500 percent (T100), and the $10.5 million note (T132).

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.reason: Asks neutrally, e.g. 'Is that accurate?' (T80), and asks how the $4.5M return fits with his earlier statement (T82) without drawing a conclusion.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.reason: Gives the witness room to explain the Foundation (T83), the LJM2 returns (T101) and the Chewco note (T137) before moving on.

missed_chances.description: Witness hedged that he 'may have said it should be resolved' after counsel doubted the $2.6M payment; this key lead on authorizing an undisclosed payment was not followed up.
missed_chances.question: After counsel said nothing was owed, did you tell anyone to make the payment? Yes or no, and who?

missed_chances.description: Witness admitted some approvals were papered after deals closed, a control failure on a key question; the interviewer did not ask which approvals or who knew.
missed_chances.question: Which approvals were signed after closing, and did Causey and Buy know the deals had already closed?

tips: When he says he may have mentioned an investment to a subordinate, ask: What exactly did you say to him, and did you ever ask him to invest?
When he calls terms market terms but says he negotiated them himself, ask: What did you personally agree with the seller, and what evidence shows those terms match the market?
